I don't have any notes for Psalm 42 yet. My first batch of page requests went over the research tool's usage limit, and that blocked any more requests in this session. So I couldn't read Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Precept Austin, Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*, Augustine's sermon on this psalm at New Advent, or any other source.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and to give a URL for every point. Writing notes from memory would break that rule, so I've left everything out rather than guess.

**What I'll do when I can search again (for example, if you ask me in a new message):**

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word (enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-42/), then Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com/commentaries/…/psalms/42.htm, Precept Austin, and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on blueletterbible.org or spurgeon.org.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, plus Ligonier, Desiring God and TGC (Reformed and Baptist) and 1517 or LCMS (Lutheran). I'll check whether they really disagree on any verse, such as v. 6–7 on the believer's spiritual depression, or v. 8, rather than assuming they do.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes (Psalm 42–43 read as one poem, the shared refrain in v. 5 and 11, the Mizar and Hermon geography in v. 6), Augustine's sermon on New Advent (in his numbering it is Psalm 41), and Catholic.com or OCA material on how the psalm is used in baptism and the liturgy.

If you'd like, ask again and I'll fetch these one at a time so I stay under the limit.
